005package org.wpilib.hardware.rotation;
006
007import org.wpilib.hardware.discrete.AnalogInput;
008import org.wpilib.system.RobotController;
009import org.wpilib.telemetry.TelemetryLoggable;
010import org.wpilib.telemetry.TelemetryTable;
011
012/**
013 * Class for reading analog potentiometers. Analog potentiometers read in an analog voltage that
014 * corresponds to a position. The position is in whichever units you choose, by way of the scaling
015 * and offset constants passed to the constructor.
016 */
017public class AnalogPotentiometer implements TelemetryLoggable, AutoCloseable {
018  private AnalogInput m_analogInput;
019  private boolean m_initAnalogInput;
020  private double m_fullRange;
021  private double m_offset;
022
023  /**
024   * AnalogPotentiometer constructor.
025   *
026   * <p>Use the fullRange and offset values so that the output produces meaningful values. I.E: you
027   * have a 270 degree potentiometer, and you want the output to be degrees with the halfway point
028   * as 0 degrees. The fullRange value is 270.0(degrees) and the offset is -135.0 since the halfway
029   * point after scaling is 135 degrees. This will calculate the result from the fullRange times the
030   * fraction of the supply voltage, plus the offset.
031   *
032   * @param channel The SmartIO channel this potentiometer is plugged into.
033   * @param fullRange The scaling to multiply the fraction by to get a meaningful unit.
034   * @param offset The offset to add to the scaled value for controlling the zero value
035   */
036  public AnalogPotentiometer(final int channel, double fullRange, double offset) {
037    this(new AnalogInput(channel), fullRange, offset);
038    m_initAnalogInput = true;
039  }
040
041  /**
042   * AnalogPotentiometer constructor.
043   *
044   * <p>Use the fullRange and offset values so that the output produces meaningful values. I.E: you
045   * have a 270 degree potentiometer, and you want the output to be degrees with the halfway point
046   * as 0 degrees. The fullRange value is 270.0(degrees) and the offset is -135.0 since the halfway
047   * point after scaling is 135 degrees. This will calculate the result from the fullRange times the
048   * fraction of the supply voltage, plus the offset.
049   *
050   * @param input The {@link AnalogInput} this potentiometer is plugged into.
051   * @param fullRange The angular value (in desired units) representing the full 0-3.3V range of the
052   *     input.
053   * @param offset The angular value (in desired units) representing the angular output at 0V.
054   */
055  public AnalogPotentiometer(final AnalogInput input, double fullRange, double offset) {
056    m_analogInput = input;
057    m_initAnalogInput = false;
058
059    m_fullRange = fullRange;
060    m_offset = offset;
061  }
062
063  /**
064   * AnalogPotentiometer constructor.
065   *
066   * <p>Use the scale value so that the output produces meaningful values. I.E: you have a 270
067   * degree potentiometer, and you want the output to be degrees with the starting point as 0
068   * degrees. The scale value is 270.0(degrees).
069   *
070   * @param channel The analog input channel this potentiometer is plugged into.
071   * @param scale The scaling to multiply the voltage by to get a meaningful unit.
072   */
073  public AnalogPotentiometer(final int channel, double scale) {
074    this(channel, scale, 0);
075  }
076
077  /**
078   * AnalogPotentiometer constructor.
079   *
080   * <p>Use the fullRange and offset values so that the output produces meaningful values. I.E: you
081   * have a 270 degree potentiometer, and you want the output to be degrees with the starting point
082   * as 0 degrees. The scale value is 270.0(degrees).
083   *
084   * @param input The {@link AnalogInput} this potentiometer is plugged into.
085   * @param scale The scaling to multiply the voltage by to get a meaningful unit.
086   */
087  public AnalogPotentiometer(final AnalogInput input, double scale) {
088    this(input, scale, 0);
089  }
090
091  /**
092   * AnalogPotentiometer constructor.
093   *
094   * <p>The potentiometer will return a value between 0 and 1.0.
095   *
096   * @param channel The analog input channel this potentiometer is plugged into.
097   */
098  public AnalogPotentiometer(final int channel) {
099    this(channel, 1, 0);
100  }
101
102  /**
103   * AnalogPotentiometer constructor.
104   *
105   * <p>The potentiometer will return a value between 0 and 1.0.
106   *
107   * @param input The {@link AnalogInput} this potentiometer is plugged into.
108   */
109  public AnalogPotentiometer(final AnalogInput input) {
110    this(input, 1, 0);
111  }
112
113  /**
114   * Get the current reading of the potentiometer.
115   *
116   * @return The current position of the potentiometer.
117   */
118  public double get() {
119    if (m_analogInput == null) {
120      return m_offset;
121    }
122    return (m_analogInput.getVoltage() / RobotController.getVoltage3V3()) * m_fullRange + m_offset;
123  }
124
125  @Override
126  public void logTo(TelemetryTable table) {
127    table.log("Value", get());
128  }
129
130  @Override
131  public String getTelemetryType() {
132    return "Analog Input";
133  }
134
135  @Override
136  public void close() {
137    if (m_analogInput != null && m_initAnalogInput) {
138      m_analogInput.close();
139    }
140    m_analogInput = null;
141  }
142}
